text: dsh-skin-claude-code 是一款面向 DSH Web 客户端的 Claude Code 风格界面皮肤。它作为浏览器端主题插件注册，在当前主题上叠加亮色和暗色两套主题令牌，并注入终端风格 CSS。它将界面底色调整为暖炭黑或暖米白，使用陶土橙强调色，统一等宽字体，并为代码块、焦点环、链接、输入光标和滚动条设置协调样式。主题效果由插件生命周期管理，停用时会清理注入的样式。适合希望让 DSH 网页界面呈现终端编辑器观感的用户；需要 DSH Web profile 和客户端主题接口，无需额外密钥或外部服务。

dsh-skin-claude-code gives DSH Web a Claude Code-inspired look with warm light and dark colors, monospace text, terracotta accents, and styled code blocks and scrollbars. It removes injected styles when stopped. Requires the DSH web theme interface; no API key or external service.
想把 DSH 网页界面换成 Claude Code 那种终端风格。
有没有适合 DSH Web 的暖色主题和陶土橙配色？
让 DSH 的代码块、输入框和滚动条看起来更像终端。
DSH 能不能跟随亮色和暗色界面切换配色？
想给网页里的文字换成 JetBrains Mono 一类的等宽字体。
Can I give the DSH web interface a warm, terminal-inspired theme?
I want matching light and dark colors for my DSH browser UI.
How can I make code blocks and scrollbars fit a monospace editor look?
dsh-skin-claude-code 的功能「双模式主题配色」：在当前 DSH 主题上覆盖界面颜色令牌，提供暖米白亮色和暖炭黑暗色配色。插件激活时应用覆盖，停用时由主题效果清理。
dsh-skin-claude-code 的功能「终端字体和强调色」：为网页正文设置等宽字体，并将选区、输入光标、焦点环和链接统一为陶土橙强调色。启用皮肤后自动应用这些浏览器样式。
dsh-skin-claude-code 的功能「代码表面与滚动条样式」：为 code 和 pre 内容设置暖色背景、边框与圆角，并统一滚动条宽度和颜色。样式由浏览器端插件注入，停止时移除。

dsh-skin-claude-code README · dsh-skin-claude-code：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A **Claude Code–inspired skin** for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) web GUI.

It restyles the browser surface with Claude Code's signature look:

dsh-skin-claude-code README · dsh-skin-claude-code：- **Warm charcoal / warm cream** surfaces instead of the stock cool grays
- **Terracotta accent** (`#D97757`) for brand, focus, caret, links, and scrollbars
- **Monospace terminal typography** (JetBrains Mono / ui-monospace fallback)
- Warm-tinted code blocks and `code`/`pre` surfaces

The skin stacks a token-override layer over whatever theme is active, so it
adapts automatically to **light**, **dark**, and **system** preferences.

dsh-skin-claude-code README · Install：The package is a DSH **bundle**: its `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`,
so `dsh plugin add` installs it **and** auto-registers it as a profile layer.
No `cordis.patch.yml` editing is required.

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-skin-claude-code
```

To target a different profile, change `--profile`. A convenience wrapper also
ships in the repo:

```sh
./install.sh            # optional profile name, defaults to "web"
```

dsh-skin-claude-code README · Why no manual patch edit：`dsh plugin add` forwards to pnpm inside the profile, then reconciles the
profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` list: a dependency whose `package.json`
declares `dsh.bundle.patch` is appended to that list automatically. On boot,
the loader applies each bundle's own `cordis.patch.yml` (which inserts the
skin's row), so the plugin mounts with no manual composition edits.

---

dsh-skin-claude-code README · Uninstall：```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-skin-claude-code
```

---

dsh-skin-claude-code README · How it works：- `package.json` declares two things:
  - `dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`, which inserts the plugin row;
  - `dsh.client` (`platform: web`, `inject` on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-theme`),
    which serves the browser half.
- `lib/index.js` is the no-op host half (client-only plugins still export a
  host entry so the composition loader can resolve the row).
- `lib/client.js` registers with `window.__ModuleLoader__`, then on activation:
  - calls `ctx.theme.overrideTokens("dsh-skin-claude-code", TOKENS)` — a
    reversible token layer over the active theme, with light/dark values;
  - injects a `<style>` element for the monospace/terminal chrome, owned by the
    Cordis fiber so stop/update/remove cleans it up.

dsh-skin-claude-code README · How it works：No product DOM selectors are used — only the public `--dsw-alias-*` theme
tokens and generic elements — so the skin degrades safely across harness
updates.

---

dsh-skin-claude-code README · Customize：Edit the `TOKENS` map and `CSS` template in `lib/client.js`, then republish (or
install from your clone). The files under `lib/` are hand-written build
artifacts, so no bundler step is required to iterate.
